question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ be I.I.D. random variables with probability density function

$$
f(x;\theta )=(\theta +1){x}^{-\theta -2},\,x\ge 1,
$$

where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter. Find the likelihood function of the sample $1.5,\,1.8,\,2.0.$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
L(\theta )=P({X}_{1}={x}_{1},{X}_{2}={x}_{2},…,{X}_{n}={x}_{n})={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\,\theta ).
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=3$ independent random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x;\theta )=(\theta +1){x}^{-\theta -2},\,x\ge 1.
$$

We can calculate the likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(\theta ) & ={\prod }_{i=1}^{n}((\theta +1){x}_{i}^{-\theta -2}) \\  & =(\theta +1)^{n}\cdot {\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{-\theta -2} \\  & =(\theta +1)^{n}({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i})^{-\theta -2}\end{aligned}
$$

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =1.5\cdot 1.8\cdot 2=5.4\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=3.$ Therefore, 

$$
L(\theta )=(\theta +1)^{3}(5.4)^{-\theta -2}.
$$
